source: Roy et al. (2024) Exploring LLM-based Agents for Root Cause Analysis
finding: A ReAct agent with retrieval tools was about as correct as strong baselines on 500 real cloud incidents, but hallucinated far less.
numbers: Correct: ReAct S+Q BM25 35% vs 39% for the best baselines (RB k=10 and CoT). Hallucination: ReAct 4%, CoT 12%, RB k=10 40%. Dataset: 107,000 incidents; 100 eval and 500 test sampled. Base LLM GPT-4. 28 of 97 cases solved by all three models.
limits: Title and description only; no team-specific tools in the main test. Metrics BLEU/ROUGE/METEOR plus a 100-prediction manual coding by two authors.
agent_relevance: Opened evidence steps (S1-S4) buy grounding, not raw accuracy. Expect lower hallucination, not a higher hit rate.

source: Roy et al. (2024) RQ1 error analysis
finding: Most ReAct failures were not made-up facts but too little evidence: the agent could not see the discriminating observation.
numbers: 66% of ReAct incorrect predictions were Insufficient Evidence. Of 38 correct predictions by RB k=10, 26% (10) contained hallucinations; of its 59 incorrect, 49% (29) did. CoT and ReAct correct predictions had under 1% hallucination.
limits: Single org (Microsoft), one error coding scheme adapted from Yao et al.
agent_relevance: A scaffold should have a 'need more evidence' exit instead of forcing a verdict from the report alone.

source: Roy et al. (2024) RQ2 discussion comments
finding: Adding past engineers' diagnostic discussion comments to the retrieval corpus did not help.
numbers: Changes in lexical metrics were tiny or negative: C-BLEU -0.13, S-BLEU -0.39, METEOR -0.7, rougeL -1 for one model; +0.1 rougeL and +0.8 METEOR for another.
limits: Gains judged small and inconsistent; semantic metrics unchanged.
agent_relevance: Past human reasoning traces are not automatically useful retrieval material.

source: Roy et al. (2024) RQ3 Azure case study
finding: With team-specific tools and a knowledge base the agent could follow runbook-style diagnosis, but it failed on tool errors and a 20-step cap.
numbers: Trajectory capped at 20 steps; the paper reports this was not enough for some incidents. Team said RCA needs over 1.5 years of experience.
limits: One team, prototype, no quantitative accuracy table found in the text read.
agent_relevance: Human-in-the-loop correction of tool failures mattered; plan an explicit recovery step for failed tests.

source: Ahmed et al. (2023) Recommending Root-Cause and Mitigation Steps for Cloud Incidents using LLMs
finding: Early large study: fine-tuned GPT-3.x beat encoder-decoder baselines and zero-shot models on root-cause text, but absolute overlap scores stayed low.
numbers: Over 40,000 incidents from 1,759 Microsoft services. Code-davinci-002 BLEU-4 4.24, ROUGE-L 11.43, METEOR 10.42 (first value in each pair), with percent gain over Davinci of 23.26, 26.44, 42.16. Root cause BLEU-4 range 3.38-4.24; mitigation 4.44-6.76. Multi-task training changed BLEU-4 by about 2.8% on average.
limits: Lexical metrics undervalue valid answers; human evaluation by incident owners is the real test. Title and description only.
agent_relevance: Models paraphrase past causes; success here is retrieval of known failure classes, not fresh diagnosis.

source: Ahmed et al. (2023) failure mode: useless recommendations
finding: Many outputs for mitigation were generic ('issue is self-mitigated', 'fix deployed to all regions') and useless to engineers.
numbers: Fine-tuned plain Davinci (175B) underperformed baselines on automatic metrics. Repeated sampling gave duplicates above 97%.
limits: Stated qualitatively in the paper; I did not see a single percentage for the generic-output share.
agent_relevance: Check outputs for specificity; reward a testable, named cause.

source: Wang, Liu et al. (2024) RCAgent: Cloud Root Cause Analysis by Autonomous Agents
finding: Plain ReAct was unstable; stability and diversity fixes (JSON repair, observation snapshots, expert sub-agents, trajectory self-consistency) did the work.
numbers: RCAgent Pass Rate 99.38% within 15 steps, Invalid Rate 7.93%. Ablations: no JSON regen 85.71% pass; no LLM experts 92.55%; with sampling only 70.19% pass and 44.80% invalid; SQL tools instead of minimal tools -33.54% pass, 70.95% invalid. Root-cause METEOR +8.71 over ReAct, falling to +3.16 without expert agents. Self-consistency gains plateau near 20 samples; LLM aggregation beat embedding voting.
limits: Alibaba Flink Advisor data, local LLM, semantic text metrics and LLM-judge G-scores.
agent_relevance: Format discipline and tool minimalism are guardrails with large measured effects. Voting over whole trajectories helps solution diversity.

source: Chen et al. (2025) AIOpsLab
finding: On an interactive microservice fault benchmark, agents did well on detection and localization and poorly on root-cause analysis and mitigation.
numbers: Overall accuracy: FLASH 59.32% (highest), ReAct 55.93%, GPT-4-with-shell 49.15%, GPT-3.5-with-shell 15.25% (lowest); the row-to-agent mapping is read from a garbled table. Detection: ReAct 76.92%, GPT-4 69.23%, GPT-3.5 23.07%. Localization Acc@1: GPT-4 61.54%, ReAct 53.85%, FLASH 46.15%. ReAct top-3 69.23% vs top-1 53.85%. GPT-3.5 mitigation 0%.
limits: Small problem set (13 detection and 13 localization problems by my reading). Single run per agent.
agent_relevance: Matches the cycle: easy to test a symptom, hard to validate a cause and to repair.

source: Chen et al. (2025) AIOpsLab step-limit and behaviour analysis
finding: More steps stop helping after about 5 steps; agents waste steps repeating the same call, breaking API formats and dumping raw telemetry.
numbers: A step limit beyond 5 gave no better accuracy, only more tokens; FLASH peaked at 59.32%. Failure classes: repeated API calls, invalid API use, apologise-and-retry loops, cat of raw telemetry.
limits: Authors contrast with code tasks where linters and tests give strong feedback; ops feedback is weak.
agent_relevance: Self-repair from environment feedback saturates fast. Add an explicit hypothesis ledger rather than more turns.

source: Jha et al. (2025) ITBench
finding: Frontier-model agents solved few real incident-style scenarios and results varied run to run.
numbers: Scenario success: SRE 13.8%, CISO 25.2%, FinOps 0%. 94 scenarios; SRE 42 scenarios, 10 runs each. GPT-4o best: SRE diagnosis pass@1 13.81%. FinOps diagnosis 33% for GPT-4o.
limits: Models are 2024-era (GPT-4o, Llama-3.x, Mistral Large); only 11 of 94 scenarios open-sourced.
agent_relevance: Real faults with partial observability are far from solved by a plain agent loop.

source: Jha et al. (2025) ITBench moderators: observability and complexity
finding: Removing trace data and raising scenario complexity both cut diagnosis sharply; outcomes were nondeterministic.
numbers: GPT-4o diagnosis 13.81% with traces vs 9.52% without; mitigation fell to 2.86% without. By complexity, diagnosis 36% Easy, 7.73% Medium, 5.0% Hard; mitigation 21%, 12.27%, 0%. SRE agent diagnosed scenario 8 in 1 of 10 runs, scenario 13 in 6 of 10, scenario 21 in 8 of 10.
limits: Complexity defined by propagation-chain length, resolution steps and technology diversity.
agent_relevance: Long fault-propagation chains are the hard part: the agent must track a multi-link causal path, not one cause. Measure over repeated runs.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) LLM-as-an-Investigator (SIA)
finding: Interactive diagnosis from forum threads: an evidence-first agent with competing-hypothesis tracking and a counterfactual challenger beat ReAct and Tree of Thoughts.
numbers: 100 cases (from 303 technical threads), final score out of 100: SIA 79.2 [72.7, 83.7]; THK-int 72.8; Ask-5 72.3; ReAct 69.0; ToT 61.5; BAS 67.3; THK 67.5. Questions asked: SIA 5.2, ReAct 2.8. Other backbones: GPT-5.6 Terra 75.4 vs 69.2; Claude Sonnet 5 76.1 vs 68.4.
limits: User simulator answers questions; the paper itself calls differences descriptive on this cohort; confidence intervals overlap for several rows. Preprint v2 dated 13 Oct 2026.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for S1-S4 as a loop: hypotheses, discriminating questions, challenge, verify.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) potential-versus-final gap
finding: Thinking of the right cause is not enough; choosing it is the weak step. Broader search (Tree of Thoughts) widened the gap.
numbers: Potential vs final: SIA 89.2 vs 79.2 (gap 10.0); ToT 84.0 vs 61.5 (gap 22.5); ReAct 86.5 vs 69.0; BAS 81.2 vs 67.3.
limits: Potential is an oracle over recorded candidates; ReAct and ToT log pruned paths so coverage is not comparable.
agent_relevance: Add a separate adjudication step after generation. Do not equate more hypotheses with better diagnosis.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) component ablation
finding: Each part of the loop mattered; structured investigation most, evidence-weight updates least.
numbers: Final score: full 79.2; no structured investigation 72.8; no counterfactual critique 74.0; no follow-up questions 75.0; no final adjudication 76.0 (potential unchanged 89.2); no hypothesis expansion 76.5 (potential falls to 79.3); no weight updates 78.5.
limits: Same 100 cases, one backbone (Gemini) for the ablation.
agent_relevance: Ranks which S-state to keep: state structure and challenge beat numeric weighting.

source: Marozzo and Lio (2026) misleading user conjecture stress test
finding: A plausible but wrong user suggestion lowered scores a little and was taken as the answer in 2 of 10 cases.
numbers: 10 paired cases: final 80.0 control vs 76.0 challenged; potential 90.0 vs 85.0; exact diagnosis 6/10 vs 5/10; suggested wrong cause selected 2/10; lower than control in 3/10.
limits: Ten cases only; no significance test.
agent_relevance: Keep user-proposed causes as hypotheses, never as evidence (guardrail against anchoring).

source: Tseng et al. (2026) SADE: Symptom-Aware Diagnostic Escalation
finding: Encoding the Cisco layer-by-layer troubleshooting method as a phase-gated policy raised network root-cause F1 well above a free-form ReAct agent.
numbers: 523 held-out incidents, 11 unseen scenarios. Root-cause F1: SADE 0.77, Claude-Code same backbone 0.55, ReAct+GPT-5 0.40 (text elsewhere says 0.44). Detection accuracy 0.85 vs 0.67 and 0.68. Judge score 4.32 vs 3.93 vs 3.80. +37 points over ReAct, of which 22 points are credited to policy alone.
limits: Internal inconsistency in ReAct F1 (0.40 vs 0.44) in the same paper; LLM-as-judge by GPT-5-mini; skill library hand-written; emulated networks.
agent_relevance: Best controlled test that a human troubleshooting method as scaffold beats free deliberation on the same model.

source: Tseng et al. (2026) SADE efficiency and reliability
finding: The gated method reached a decision more often and with fewer probes per correct answer.
numbers: No-submission rate: SADE 4.2%, ReAct 8.8%, Claude-Code 15.3% (80 cases down to 22). Tool calls per session 19.9 vs 25.4 vs 26.7; per correct submission 27.2 vs 49.5 vs 51.5. Cost per session about $1.44 SADE vs $0.20 ReAct vs $0.83 Claude-Code. Claude-Code baseline fell on larger topologies; SADE did not.
limits: SADE costs more tokens (median input about 483k vs 89k for ReAct, by my reading of the table).
agent_relevance: An explicit termination point matters. Budget tokens, not only steps.

source: Li et al. (2026) QoEReasoner
finding: Radio-network fault diagnosis with deterministic tools, a knowledge base and a case bank; plain LLMs struggle with numeric telemetry and hallucinate.
numbers: Cumulative hit rate figures read near 74-76% on two backbones (DeepSeek-V3.2 and GPT-5.2); about 20% of cases go through hypothesis Expansion and about 80% Reconfigured.
limits: I read the abstract, intro and parts of results only; figure and ablation values are partly garbled in text extraction, so treat numbers as approximate.
agent_relevance: Keep numbers in deterministic tools; let the model reason over structured evidence.

source: Mamede et al. (2020) Immunising physicians against availability bias (BMJ Qual Saf)
finding: Teaching discriminating features (knowledge) protected residents from a bias induced a week earlier; a human diagnostic-error analogue of troubleshooting.
numbers: N=91 residents, 8 hospitals. On biased vignettes immunised 0.40 vs 0.24 (diff 0.16, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.27, p=0.004); unbiased vignettes 0.36 vs 0.41 (p=0.45). Non-immunised dropped 0.17 on biased cases (p=0.005).
limits: Simulated vignettes, medicine not equipment, residents only, accuracy low overall (0.24-0.41).
agent_relevance: Give the agent the discriminating features of look-alike faults, not generic 'think carefully' text.

source: Mamede et al. (2021) Disease knowledge predicts susceptibility to availability bias (J Gen Intern Med)
finding: Residents who knew the discriminating findings were far less biased by recent exposure.
numbers: N=62 residents. Biased diagnoses per participant (range 0-4): higher-knowledge 0.35 vs lower-knowledge 0.97, difference 0.62 (95% CI 0.28-0.95, p=0.001). Both groups slowed on biased cases (p=0.04).
limits: Knowledge measured by 2-second feature decisions; correlational split; residents only.
agent_relevance: Bias resistance is a knowledge effect; retrieval of fault-specific features matters more than process steps.

source: Lambe, Hevey and Kelly (2018) Guided reflection shows no effect on diagnostic accuracy (Front Psychol)
finding: Failed replication of the benefit of guided reflection with novices: no gain in accuracy, confidence change or corrected diagnoses.
numbers: N=186 4th and 5th year medical students; control first impression vs short (2 alternatives) vs long (6 alternatives) reflection. No accuracy difference between any conditions; short equalled long.
limits: Novices, fictional cases. Authors suggest novices already reason analytically.
agent_relevance: A generate-alternatives prompt is not a free win. Its value depends on problem difficulty relative to knowledge.

source: Availability bias and reflection in internal medicine residents (2020, PMC7807127)
finding: Recent exposure to dengue caused misdiagnosis of look-alikes, and reflecting afterwards did not repair it.
numbers: N=46 residents. Control scored 0.80 on dengue-lookalike vs 0.59 filler cases (p<0.01); exposed group 0.66 vs 0.64 (p=0.756). Wrong-as-dengue 71-100% in exposed group. Reflective re-diagnosis no better than non-analytic in any case.
limits: Small sample, single disease, six-hour gap. Author list and journal not recorded in my notes.
agent_relevance: Reflection fails when the wrong hypothesis came from context; the remedy is new discriminating evidence.

source: Mamede and Schmidt (2023) Deliberate reflection and clinical reasoning: founding ideas and empirical findings
finding: Deliberate reflection helps on hard cases for experienced people, can hurt novices on hard cases, and one study failed to find the effect.
numbers: Residents improved by more than 35% with deliberate reflection on complex cases, no change on simple ones; students benefited on simple cases and did worse reflecting on complex ones. A version asking for features for and against each diagnosis found no benefit; the authors reply it needs bottom-up sequential hypotheses.
limits: Narrative review by people close to the method; effect depends on how reflection is instructed. Authorship on this line is from memory, verify.
agent_relevance: Gate extra deliberation by estimated difficulty, not always on.

source: Jonassen and Hung (2006) Learning to troubleshoot: a new theory-based design architecture
finding: Key cited source for this subfield; not opened this session because web search quota was used up and the paper is paywalled.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Not read. Do not cite numbers from this line.
agent_relevance: Needs a second pass by an agent with search access.

source: Schaafstal, Schraagen and van Berlo (2000) structured troubleshooting training
finding: Founding training study named in the task; not opened.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Not read. Do not cite numbers from this line. DOI not verified.
agent_relevance: Needs a second pass: expert vs novice data and training effect sizes are the missing core.
